review_notes:
I read the whole file. The main candidates were `Submodule.colon` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Colon.lean and `Submodule.div` (`I / J`, `mem_div_iff_forall_mul_mem`) in Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Operations.lean.

`Submodule.colon` gives an ideal of the ring acting on the module. For the conductor, `N` would have to be an S-submodule of S, but `R<x>` is only an R-submodule. So `colon` would produce an ideal of R, not the S-ideal `conductor R x`. That is a different concept, not a duplicate.

`Submodule.div` on `Submodule R S` would give `R<x> / ⊤` as an R-submodule. The conductor is the same set, but it is packaged as an `Ideal S`. Mathlib has no existing `Ideal S` form of it, and the rest of the file and its users depend on that form. Examples are `Ideal.comap`, `Ideal.map` and quotients, plus the uses in KummerDedekind and ZariskisMainTheorem. `conductor` is also a named specialisation with its own API, so I did not find a justified consolidation.

The other declarations are lemmas, an equivalence and a localization lemma. They do not compete with any Mathlib concept I found. I could not execute Lean. I searched for an existing conductor definition in Mathlib/RingTheory but did not check the whole library exhaustively.
